news.title: [SMM Analysis] Zimbabwe's lithium landscape: rapidly growing export & accelerating local downstream processing policyZimbabwe's lithium products have emerged as a leading source of export earnings for the country, with the Minerals Marketing Corporation of Zimbabwe (MMCZ) reporting significant growth in sales. At the same time, as the January 2027 ban on lithium concentrate exports approaches, a gap is emerging between the construction timelines of local downstream processing projects and the requirements of government policy, raising concerns over the continuity and structure of lithium raw material supply. Concentrates still dominant, with sales up368% According to data disclosed by MMCZ on October 8, total mineral product export sales in Zimbabwe reached US$4.735 billion between January and September 2026, up 101.8% year on year. Lithium product sales accounted for approximately US$2.159 billion, or 45.6% of mineral export sales within the reporting scope, surpassing platinum group metals to become one of the country's largest sources of mineral export revenue. By product, spodumene concentrate sales reached roughly US$1.812 billion, up 368.2% year on year, accounting for about 83.9% of total lithium product sales. Over the same period, petalite sales stood at approximately US$155 million, up 583.3%, while lithium sulphate sales reached about US$191 million on sales volume of 33,807 tonnes — a category that recorded no sales in the corresponding period of 2025. In terms of pricing, Zimbabwe realised an average selling price of approximately US$1,483 per tonne for spodumene concentrate in the first three quarters, up from US$387 per tonne a year earlier, an increase of roughly 283%. This indicates that the marked growth in lithium export revenue was driven not only by changes in export volume but also by a sharp rise in concentrate prices. In terms of the export mix, although commercial exports of lithium sulphate have made progress, spodumene concentrate remains the main source of revenue. By value, spodumene concentrate and petalite together accounted for about 91.1% of lithium product sales, reflecting that Zimbabwe's lithium industry remains in a transitional stage of shifting from concentrate exports towards domestic downstream processing. Bikita lithium sulphate project delayed; companies seek extension of policy transition period With lithium export revenue growing rapidly, Zimbabwe's local processing policy has entered a critical implementation phase. According to local media reports on October 9, Bikita Minerals, a subsidiary of Sinomine Resource Group, has engaged with the government over the restrictions on lithium concentrate exports slated for early 2027, seeking additional time to transition. Bikita is building a lithium sulphate plant with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, involving an investment of approximately US$400 million. The project was originally scheduled for completion in March 2027, but equipment transportation delays and supply chain factors have pushed the expected start of operations to July 2027 — later than the planned implementation date of the concentrate export restrictions. The company has also asked the government to reconsider the arrangement of export-related taxes and royalties in order to ease the operational pressure created by capital expenditure and lithium price volatility. In addition, Bikita said that once the export quota system is introduced, certain mineral products are piling up at the mine site, creating pressure on existing storage capacity. This means that even where mines have the capacity to maintain production, actual export volumes may still be constrained by export quotas and storage and logistics conditions. Government reaffirms 2027 ban timeline; local processing capacity transition remains challenging In response to the companies' requests for a delay, the Zimbabwean government has maintained its position of advancing domestic processing. On October 9, Zimbabwe's Minister of Information Nick Mangwana said that the relevant lithium mining companies had already been given sufficient time to prepare local processing facilities, and there was no reason to delay the lithium concentrate export ban scheduled for January 2027. In February 2026, Zimbabwe suspended lithium concentrate exports, before partially restoring them in April through a company quota management system. However, the policy direction of fully restricting concentrate exports in 2027 has not formally changed. At present, Huayou Cobalt's Arcadia project has achieved commercial production and exports of lithium sulphate, while mines including Bikita, Kamativi and Sabi Star remain at the construction or planning stage for local processing projects. Given the differing commissioning timelines across these projects, whether local lithium sulphate processing capacity can absorb existing concentrate output in early 2027 remains to be seen. Export growth alongside policy restrictions: structural adjustment ahead for China's lithium raw material supply Zimbabwe is one of the key source countries for China's imported lithium concentrate, and changes to its export policy will directly affect overseas raw material procurement arrangements for Chinese lithium salt producers. The data for the first three quarters of 2026 shows that Zimbabwe's lithium concentrate exports still maintained a substantial commercial scale. While lithium sulphate exports have begun to contribute incremental volume, the product mix remains dominated by concentrate. In the near term, lithium concentrate exports from Zimbabwe in the fourth quarter of 2026 will continue to be affected by the existing quota system and actual logistics conditions. For Chinese lithium salt companies, the pace of arrivals will depend not only on mine output but also on export permits, port shipments and transport cycles. Entering 2027, if Zimbabwe strictly enforces the concentrate export ban on the original timetable while some lithium sulphate projects have yet to reach stable production, the country's lithium raw material exports could face temporary supply continuity pressure during the transition from concentrate to lithium sulphate. For the Chinese market, changes in concentrate arrival volumes may affect the raw material procurement structure of some lithium salt producers and cause short-term disturbances to spodumene concentrate prices. The actual price impact, however, will depend on the strength of policy implementation, supply growth from other source countries, raw material inventories at Chinese ports and smelters, and changes in downstream lithium salt demand. Overall, Zimbabwe's lithium industry sits at the intersection of rapid export revenue growth and accelerating local downstream processing policy. Over the coming months, whether the government introduces transitional export arrangements, the actual construction progress of projects such as Bikita, and changes in the export mix between concentrate and lithium sulphate will be key indicators for assessing China's lithium raw material supply in 2027.Oct 12, 2026 22:18 (GMT+8)

news.title: [SMM Analysis] Weak Demand Expectations Dominate, Spot Lithium Carbonate Falls Below the 110,000 Yuan MarkOn Oct 12, SMM quoted spot battery-grade lithium carbonate at 111,500-119,300 yuan/mt, with an average price of 115,400 yuan/mt, a sharp drop of 6,950 yuan/mt from the previous working day, or about 5.7%, marking a heavy single-day slump. The most-traded lithium carbonate futures contract 2701 opened lower and moved lower, hitting an intraday low of 105,320 yuan/mt, with the largest intraday decline once approaching 11%. Open interest stood at 440,000 lots, up by about 17,000 lots, showing a pattern of falling prices on rising volume and open interest. 1. Market news: Demand expectations and mid-term supply expectations both took a hit 1. The EU plans to adopt safeguard measures to cut annual imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles by about half from an estimated 800,000 units in 2026. The first-year cap would be about 350,000 units, rising 6% each year from the second year, with the measures lasting four years. Additional tariffs may be imposed on volumes exceeding the quota. If approved, the measures would take effect as early as Dec 1, 2026. The restricted models are mainly LFP hybrids, and the news directly dented market confidence in the sustainability of LFP demand. 2. In September, domestic retail sales of passenger NEVs reached 1.084 million units, down 16.7% YoY and up 7.8% MoM. From January to September, retail sales of passenger NEVs totaled 7.758 million units, down 12.8% YoY. 3. Expectations of mid-term supply recovery are building. Expectations of production resumptions at overseas mines and the release of new capacity remain in place. Lithium Africa recently announced it is advancing the Springbok lithium project in South Africa, with first production of spodumene concentrates planned for H2 2027. Jiangxi Special Electric Motor announced on Oct 11 that it had received a review opinion from the National Mine Safety Administration, agreeing in principle to approve the safety facility design for its Xikeng lithium mine with a mining capacity of 3 million mt/year. The mine has a theoretical LCE capacity of about 20,000 mt/year. Meanwhile, the Yichun Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau again issued a public notice on Oct 8 regarding the proposed acceptance of the environmental assessment for the Jianxiawo lithium mine. 2. Supply-demand fundamentals: Limited near-term supply growth; steady production schedules during peak demand season On the supply side, according to SMM data, lithium carbonate production last week was 25,418 mt, down 523 mt WoW, with production from spodumene-based lithium extraction, salt lake lithium extraction, and recycling-based lithium extraction all declining to varying degrees. October production schedules, including lithium extraction from slag, are expected to be 118,000 mt, with limited growth. On the demand side, production schedules during the peak season remain steady. In October, SMM total battery cell production schedules are about 320 GWh, up about 6% MoM. LFP cathode material production schedules are about 500,000 mt, up about 4% MoM. Ternary cathode material production schedules are about 84,000 mt, up about 3% MoM. Demand data itself is not weak, and the supply-demand pattern remains tight. However, the current demand peak season has been fully priced in by the market, and the pricing focus of futures has shifted to supply and demand expectations for next year. Inventory: destocking continued. As of October 8, SMM total inventory stood at 139,517 mt, down 9,260 mt from before the holiday. The destocking was mainly driven by cathode plant absorption (down 8,347 mt MoM), with the trade segment also destocking (down 1,445 mt), while upstream inventory edged up 201 mt. The absolute inventory level continued to converge toward the low end, providing some support to spot prices. III. Market Outlook Today's increase in open interest alongside price declines indicates that bears are actively entering the market, and consensus on the downside direction is strengthening. After lithium carbonate prices broke below the 110,000 yuan level, the bearish technical pattern has been established. In the short term, lithium carbonate prices are likely to remain in the doldrums, with the 100,000 yuan/mt level becoming the next important period to watch. Looking ahead, several key variables: 1. Whether cost support near 100,000 yuan/mt and salt plants' willingness to hold prices firm can form effective resistance. 2. The realization of downstream production schedules in October and November and the sustainability of post-holiday restocking. LFP orders are currently the most important bullish logic. 3. After the seasonal slowdown in Australian ore shipments and arrivals in October, whether port and trade inventories can continue to destock.Oct 12, 2026 14:16 (GMT+8)

news.title: Gold: Morgan Stanley Says Upside Potential Far Outweighs Downside – $4,000 as SupportOctober 2, 2026 The price of gold is currently consolidating—but for forward-thinking commodity investors, this very environment presents a strategic opportunity. While high bond yields and a strong U.S. dollar are cooling the market somewhat in the short term, Morgan Stanley is already looking at the big picture: The fundamental demand base remains intact. Analysts at the U.S. investment bank therefore maintain a clear target: By the second half of 2027, the price of gold will once again break through the magic mark of $5,000 per ounce. Morgan Stanley Analysis: Why the $5,000 Target Is Coming Into Focus Amy Gower, Head of Metals and Mining Strategy at Morgan Stanley, sees the market as exceptionally well-protected on the downside despite current macro headwinds—such as high oil prices and new 20-year highs in long-term bond yields. A level above $4,000 provides a massive support line. The reason the precious metal is not reacting more strongly to rising interest rates, she explains, lies in an unusually robust base of buyers that is stabilizing the current price level. This structural strength of the market rests on three key pillars: Asian appetite for gold: Physical demand from China is extremely high. The People’s Republic’s gold imports are on track to reach their highest level since 2017—if not a long-term record. Following the brief lull during “Golden Week,” this buying power is likely to return to the market quickly. Central banks as long-distance runners: In addition to China, other central banks—such as Poland’s—are also acting as major buyers to hedge against currency risks and concerns about the long-term sustainability of global debt mountains. Stable ETF inflows: Contrary to the classic pattern seen during periods of tight monetary policy, exchange-traded gold funds continue to expand their holdings—a remarkable sign of institutional strength, according to Morgan Stanley. Short-term selling spikes, such as those observed recently, are currently attributed primarily to portfolio rebalancing by algorithmic trading funds. Silver Follows the Fundamental Gold Trend This strong underlying trend is also spilling over into the silver market. According to experts at Morgan Stanley, silver currently correlates much more strongly with its “big brother” gold than with industrial metals such as copper. Although industrial demand—particularly from the solar industry following last year’s extreme price spikes—has cooled slightly due to material cost-cutting measures, the overarching macroeconomic potential for precious metals remains high. Ultimately, the fiscal sustainability of major economies and long-term protection against inflation remain enduring catalysts for tangible assets.
